slides.1.title: The shape of the D3 exam
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Day one: theory
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Two open-response papers: 2 hours and 80 minutes, 3 hours 20 minutes in total
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Day two: tasting
slides.1.highlights.1.content: A blind tasting of 12 wines split into two 1½-hour papers, 3 hours in total
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Check the latest official spec
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Summarised from Napa Valley Wine Academy; the format may change, so rely on official WSET documents
slides.1.content: Greece typically appears in both theory and tasting among the wider world regions, so prepare both facts and comparisons.
slides.2.title: Blind-tasting clue table for Greek wines
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Assyrtiko (Santorini)
slides.2.highlights.0.content: High acid, strong mineral and saline notes, medium to full body; Nykteri adds oak
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Moschofilero
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Pale lemon-pink, rose and jasmine, low alcohol, vibrant acid
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Malagousia
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Peach, mango, citrus; fuller than Moschofilero
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Xinomavro
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Pale and quick to brick, high acid and tannin, ageworthy
slides.2.highlights.4.title: Agiorgitiko
slides.2.highlights.4.content: Soft and fruity, with a wide style range by altitude and winemaking
slides.2.highlights.5.title: Retsina
slides.2.highlights.5.content: Clear pine-resin aroma, often on a Savatiano base
slides.2.content: Write clues as observation → inference, e.g. "high acid + saline + mineral → Assyrtiko on volcanic soil".
slides.3.title: Essay structure and common question types
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Structure
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Definition → 2–3 points (each with a Greek example and figure) → contrast/limits → conclusion
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Type 1: regional character
slides.3.highlights.1.content: e.g. how Santorini's terroir shapes Assyrtiko
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Type 2: regulation and market
slides.3.highlights.2.content: e.g. the effect of a low PDO/PGI share on Greek wine
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Type 3: climate and sustainability
slides.3.highlights.3.content: e.g. Santorini's drought and adaptation strategies
slides.3.content: Practice: sketch a skeleton for each type in 5 minutes (points and examples only), then write one in full.
slides.4.title: Time allocation and self-check
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Skeleton first
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Spend a little time listing points per question to avoid drifting
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Checklist
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Examples? Figures with years? A contrast? Consistent spellings?
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Review afterwards
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Set your own questions of these types and correct against official sources

slides.5.title: Short-answer practice: question and marking points
slides.5.highlights.0.title: Question 1
slides.5.highlights.0.content: “Explain how Santorini’s environment shapes the viticulture and style of Assyrtiko.” (about 250 words)
slides.5.highlights.1.title: Marking points for question 1
slides.5.highlights.1.content: ① strong winds → low kouloura basket training; ② little rain → dry farming, morning fog as moisture; ③ volcanic sandy, potassium-poor soils → low yields, pH as low as 2.7–2.8, high acidity and saline minerality; ④ phylloxera cannot survive → ungrafted old vines; ⑤ styles: dry white, Nykteri, Vinsanto; ⑥ limits: the 2023–2025 drought cut output from about 2,500 t to about 500 t
slides.5.highlights.2.title: Question 2
slides.5.highlights.2.content: “PDO and PGI wines make up a low share of Greek production. Assess the consequences for the Greek wine industry.” (about 350 words)
slides.5.highlights.3.title: Marking points for question 2
slides.5.highlights.3.content: ① facts: PDO + PGI about 30% versus over 80% in most other EU producers; bulk about half the home market; ② consequences: low international recognition, low price positioning, hard brand communication; ③ counterpoint: PGI gives quality estates freedom of variety and blending (e.g. Epanomi, Aegean Sea), so it is not necessarily a weakness; ④ 86.6% of exports go to the EU; ⑤ conclusion: the problem is less the system than the bulk share and weak branding
slides.5.content: The skeleton of a Santorini answer is the gr-l3-1 chain: wind → training; drought and sand → low yields and concentration; no phylloxera → old vines.
